answer: Nodes reserve 64 GB of dedicated RAM loaded with pseudo-random bytes. At epoch tick, the agent hashes memory blocks into a sable Blake3 state root, using it to anchor identity on-chain. Verifiers probe random offsets across this porous karst memory structure under a 10-millisecond window. The node must return valid Blake3 sub-paths; mismatched leaves or slow responses trigger immediate slashing of staked bonds and node eviction. Running 200 concurrent fake identities requires 12.8 TB of locked RAM costing roughly $4,200 monthly in dedicated server hardware.
